title: Reckoning
intent: He faces what he left unfinished.
emotionalTurn: Repair becomes the decision, not a speech about it.
openingImage: enters the workshop and surveys tools left in place
closingImage: glues and clamps the chair joint, and waits

shots.action: enters the workshop and surveys tools left in place
shots.lockedLookBlock: Desaturated late-light realism, warm practical lamps against cold blue-grey daylight, muted earth palette of rust, faded denim, worn wood and grey sky, locked-off camera with slow push-ins only, 35mm normal lens feel, soft natural grain, no drone shots, no saturated color.

lockedCharacterBlocks.The Man: a weathered man in his late 60s with short grey hair, a lined face, a worn brown work jacket over a faded denim shirt, dark trousers and scuffed boots, moving slowly and deliberately

shots.background: Foreground: workshop doorway and threshold. Midground: the man entering the workshop. Deep background: workshop interior with tools left in place on benches and walls, dust in light beams.
shots.choreography: Beat 1 (0-3s): man opens the workshop door and steps in. Beat 2 (3-7s): he surveys the tools left in place, turning slowly. Beat 3, payoff (7-10s): hold on his survey — returning to work left undone, not discovering a new place.
shots.cameraChoreography: Locked-off: camera does not move, wide framing with the workshop's full interior visible, so the tools left in place read as a set, not as props.
shots.lighting: Late light through workshop windows, dust in light beams, tools in warm light, corners in shadow.
shots.focus: Deep focus: man, benches, and tools all readable.
shots.motion: Subject motion: enter, turn, survey, hold. Background motion: dust in light beams. Camera still — the workshop is the subject as much as the man.
shots.extras: No background performers; the workshop is empty.
shots.loreNotes: Workshop rule: tools left in place, not moved between shots except when the man moves them to work. This is work left undone, not abandonment.

departments.production-design: Tools on benches and walls must be the same tools in s10-s16, in the same places unless the man moves them
departments.costume: Jacket unchanged, sawdust not yet on it in this shot
departments.sound: Door creak, dust in light, no music

shots.action: runs a hand along the unfinished chair rail
shots.lockedLookBlock: Desaturated late-light realism, warm practical lamps against cold blue-grey daylight, muted earth palette of rust, faded denim, worn wood and grey sky, locked-off camera with slow push-ins only, 35mm normal lens feel, soft natural grain, no drone shots, no saturated color.

lockedCharacterBlocks.The Man: a weathered man in his late 60s with short grey hair, a lined face, a worn brown work jacket over a faded denim shirt, dark trousers and scuffed boots, moving slowly and deliberately

shots.background: Foreground: workshop bench edge and wood shavings. Midground: the half-finished wooden chair. Deep background: workshop tools and window light, out of focus, so the chair is the only readable object.
shots.choreography: Beat 1 (0-3s): man's hand enters frame and finds the chair rail. Beat 2 (3-7s): his hand runs along the unfinished rail, slowly. Beat 3, payoff (7-10s): hold on the hand on the rail — recognition, not inspection.
shots.cameraChoreography: Push-in: from a close shot at 2 metres to a closer framing at 1 metre, ending on the hand and the rail.
shots.lighting: Workshop window light on the chair rail, hand in warm light, background tools in shadow.
shots.focus: Shallow focus: hand and rail sharp, workshop behind blurred.
shots.motion: Subject motion: hand finding, running along, holding. Background motion: dust in light. Camera pushes in slowly, matching the hand's pace.
shots.extras: No background performers; the workshop is empty except for the man.
shots.loreNotes: Chair rule: half-finished at the start, finished only at s17-s18. Never a different chair, never a bought chair, never finished early.

departments.production-design: Chair rail must be visibly unfinished — raw wood, no finish, no seat yet
departments.costume: Jacket sleeve and hand, sawdust beginning
departments.sound: Wood grain, his breath, no music

shots.action: planes a board slowly, shavings curling
shots.lockedLookBlock: Desaturated late-light realism, warm practical lamps against cold blue-grey daylight, muted earth palette of rust, faded denim, worn wood and grey sky, locked-off camera with slow push-ins only, 35mm normal lens feel, soft natural grain, no drone shots, no saturated color.

lockedCharacterBlocks.The Man: a weathered man in his late 60s with short grey hair, a lined face, a worn brown work jacket over a faded denim shirt, dark trousers and scuffed boots, moving slowly and deliberately

shots.background: Foreground: wood plane and a curling shaving, extreme close. Midground: the man's hands holding the plane. Deep background: workshop bench, out of focus.
shots.choreography: Beat 1 (0-3s): hands set the plane on the board. Beat 2 (3-7s): plane moves slowly along the board, shavings curling. Beat 3, payoff (7-10s): hold on the curling shaving — patience as action, the work itself as the beat.
shots.cameraChoreography: Locked-off: camera does not move, extreme close framing on the hands, plane, and shaving, so the work's rhythm reads.
shots.lighting: Workshop window light on the hands and board, shavings catching the light, background in shadow.
shots.focus: Shallow focus: plane and shaving sharp, hands slightly soft at the edges.
shots.motion: Subject motion: slow, rhythmic planing, one stroke per few seconds. Background motion: shavings curling and falling. Camera still — rhythm is in the hands, not the camera.
shots.extras: No background performers; the workshop is empty except for the man's hands.
shots.loreNotes: Work rule: patience as action. Planing is not a montage shortcut; it is shown at its real, slow pace, because the pace is the character.

departments.production-design: Board and plane must match s10's chair materials — same wood, same workshop
departments.costume: Hands and jacket sleeves, sawdust on them
departments.sound: Plane on wood, rhythmic, no music

shots.action: reads an unsent letter, then folds it carefully
shots.emotionalBeat: choosing not to destroy the past
shots.lockedLookBlock: Desaturated late-light realism, warm practical lamps against cold blue-grey daylight, muted earth palette of rust, faded denim, worn wood and grey sky, locked-off camera with slow push-ins only, 35mm normal lens feel, soft natural grain, no drone shots, no saturated color.

lockedCharacterBlocks.The Man: a weathered man in his late 60s with short grey hair, a lined face, a worn brown work jacket over a faded denim shirt, dark trousers and scuffed boots, moving slowly and deliberately

shots.background: Foreground: workshop bench with paper and a pencil. Midground: the man reading the unsent letter. Deep background: workshop tools and window, out of focus.
shots.choreography: Beat 1 (0-4s): man reads the letter, eyes moving across the page. Beat 2 (4-8s): he folds the letter carefully, in two precise folds. Beat 3, payoff (8-10s): he holds the folded letter, not tearing it, hold on the choice not to destroy the past.
shots.cameraChoreography: Locked-off: camera does not move, medium framing on the man and the letter, so reading and folding read as two beats and the hold as a third.
shots.lighting: Workshop window light on the letter paper, man's face in soft side light, background in shadow.
shots.focus: Focus on the letter in beat 1, on the man's hands in beat 2, on his face in the hold.
shots.motion: Subject motion: reading, folding, holding — three sequential beats, not simultaneous actions. Background motion: dust in light. Camera still.
shots.extras: No background performers; the workshop is empty.
shots.loreNotes: Letter rule: unsent, read once, folded carefully, never torn, never mailed, never read aloud. The choice not to destroy it is the midpoint reversal.

departments.production-design: Letter paper must be the same paper in any later shot where it appears, folded, never torn
departments.sound: Paper, silence — silence after folding is the beat, not an absence

shots.action: looks at the silent telephone and turns back to the work
shots.location: a telephone on a wall, silent
shots.lockedLookBlock: Desaturated late-light realism, warm practical lamps against cold blue-grey daylight, muted earth palette of rust, faded denim, worn wood and grey sky, locked-off camera with slow push-ins only, 35mm normal lens feel, soft natural grain, no drone shots, no saturated color.

lockedCharacterBlocks.The Man: a weathered man in his late 60s with short grey hair, a lined face, a worn brown work jacket over a faded denim shirt, dark trousers and scuffed boots, moving slowly and deliberately

shots.background: Foreground: wall beside the telephone, faded paint. Midground: the silent telephone on the wall. Deep background: workshop doorway, out of focus.
shots.choreography: Beat 1 (0-3s): man looks at the telephone. Beat 2 (3-7s): he stands, looking, not reaching for it. Beat 3, payoff (7-10s): he turns back to the work, hold on turning away — no call will fix this.
shots.cameraChoreography: Locked-off: camera does not move, close framing on the telephone and the man's face beside it.
shots.lighting: Workshop light on the telephone, man's face in shadow, no artificial light.
shots.focus: Focus on the telephone in beat 1, on the man's face in beat 3.
shots.motion: Subject motion: look, stand, turn — three small moves. Background motion: none. Camera still — the beat is a decision not to act.
shots.extras: No background performers; the workshop is empty.
shots.loreNotes: Telephone rule: silent, looked at here and turned away from. No call is made, no call arrives. The rule is: no call will fix this.

departments.production-design: Telephone on the same hallway/workshop wall system as the photograph and mirror, but a distinct wall section

shots.action: watches rain on the workshop window, tools waiting behind him
shots.emotionalBeat: weather as feeling, not metaphor forced
shots.lockedLookBlock: Desaturated late-light realism, warm practical lamps against cold blue-grey daylight, muted earth palette of rust, faded denim, worn wood and grey sky, locked-off camera with slow push-ins only, 35mm normal lens feel, soft natural grain, no drone shots, no saturated color.

lockedCharacterBlocks.The Man: a weathered man in his late 60s with short grey hair, a lined face, a worn brown work jacket over a faded denim shirt, dark trousers and scuffed boots, moving slowly and deliberately

shots.background: Foreground: workshop window frame and rain on glass. Midground: the man watching the window. Deep background: workshop tools waiting behind him, out of focus.
shots.choreography: Beat 1 (0-3s): man stands at the window, watching rain. Beat 2 (3-7s): rain runs down the glass, man still. Beat 3, payoff (7-10s): hold on watching — weather as feeling, not a metaphor forced by narration or music.
shots.cameraChoreography: Locked-off: camera does not move, wide framing with the window, the man, and the tools behind him in one composition.
shots.lighting: Grey rain light through the window, man's face in cool light, workshop behind him in shadow.
shots.focus: Focus on the rain on glass in beat 1, on the man's face in beat 3.
shots.motion: Subject motion: standing and watching, almost none. Background motion: rain on glass, the only large movement. Camera still.
shots.extras: No background performers; the workshop is empty.
shots.loreNotes: Weather rule: rain in the reckoning sequence, not in arrival or release. Weather progresses with the story's clock, it does not reset.

departments.production-design: Workshop window is the same window as s09's light source, now in rain
departments.costume: Jacket damp at the shoulders from the workshop door, not soaked

shots.action: looks at himself in the mirror, honestly, without flinching
shots.lockedLookBlock: Desaturated late-light realism, warm practical lamps against cold blue-grey daylight, muted earth palette of rust, faded denim, worn wood and grey sky, locked-off camera with slow push-ins only, 35mm normal lens feel, soft natural grain, no drone shots, no saturated color.

lockedCharacterBlocks.The Man: a weathered man in his late 60s with short grey hair, a lined face, a worn brown work jacket over a faded denim shirt, dark trousers and scuffed boots, moving slowly and deliberately

shots.background: Foreground: hallway mirror frame, worn wood. Midground: the man's reflection in the mirror. Deep background: hallway behind him in the mirror, out of focus.
shots.choreography: Beat 1 (0-3s): man looks at himself in the mirror. Beat 2 (3-7s): he looks honestly, without flinching, face still. Beat 3, payoff (7-10s): hold on the reflection — self-reckoning, not vanity, not performance.
shots.cameraChoreography: Push-in: from a medium close shot at 2 metres to a closer framing at 1 metre, ending on the reflection's face.
shots.lighting: Hallway light on the mirror, reflection lit, man's back in shadow, no artificial light.
shots.focus: Focus on the reflection, never on the man's back — the audience sees the face he sees.
shots.motion: Subject motion: look, hold, hold longer. Background motion: none. Camera pushes in slowly, matching the reckoning's pace.
shots.extras: No background performers; the hallway is empty.
shots.loreNotes: Mirror rule: the man looks at himself honestly, without flinching. The mirror is not used for exposition, and the reflection is never a different face.

departments.production-design: Mirror on the hallway wall, distinct from the photograph wall, same hallway layout
departments.costume: Jacket and face in reflection, unchanged

shots.action: glues and clamps the chair joint, then waits
shots.location: a workshop bench with glue and clamps
shots.lockedLookBlock: Desaturated late-light realism, warm practical lamps against cold blue-grey daylight, muted earth palette of rust, faded denim, worn wood and grey sky, locked-off camera with slow push-ins only, 35mm normal lens feel, soft natural grain, no drone shots, no saturated color.

lockedCharacterBlocks.The Man: a weathered man in his late 60s with short grey hair, a lined face, a worn brown work jacket over a faded denim shirt, dark trousers and scuffed boots, moving slowly and deliberately

shots.background: Foreground: workshop bench with glue bottle and clamps. Midground: the man's hands gluing and clamping the chair joint. Deep background: workshop tools, out of focus.
shots.choreography: Beat 1 (0-3s): hands apply glue to the chair joint, carefully. Beat 2 (3-7s): hands set the clamp on the joint and tighten it, one click. Beat 3, payoff (7-10s): hands rest on the clamped joint, waiting, hold on the first repair waiting to set.
shots.cameraChoreography: Locked-off: camera does not move, medium framing on the bench, hands, and joint, so gluing, clamping, and waiting read as sequential beats.
shots.lighting: Workshop window light on the bench and joint, hands in warm light, background in shadow.
shots.focus: Focus on the joint throughout, hands sharp, background blurred.
shots.motion: Subject motion: glue, clamp, wait — sequential, not simultaneous. Background motion: dust in light. Camera still — waiting is the beat.
shots.extras: No background performers; the workshop is empty except for the man's hands.
shots.loreNotes: Chair rule: the first repair. The joint clamped here must be the joint finished in s17-s18, not a different joint.

departments.production-design: Glue and clamps must be the same tools as s09's workshop set
departments.sound: Clamp click, room tone, no music
